newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Stena sees possible EU conditions on P&O deal.
newsitem.headline: Stena sees possible EU conditions on P&O deal.

text.p: Ferry operators Stena Line AB and the Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Company (P&O) may need to meet certain conditions to win European Commission clearance for their planned joint venture, a senior Stena official said on Thursday.
But Anders Hedberg, senior vice president for finance, said it would be a major surprise if the European Union executive rejected the deal.

Hedberg was responding to questions following reports that the European Commission could raise doubts next week over the proposed joint venture between the two ferry firms. Hedberg stressed that he had not heard about this from the Commission.
But, he told reporters, "we can not start cooperation unless we have full support from the authorities."

"We are talking (about) a theoretical thing now, but of course we realise that a possible okey from the authorities could mean that we also have to...meet up to certain conditions which is quite common in competition cases."
"So there might be some restrictions. That would not be a surprise," he said. However, a 'no' from the Commission would be a "big surprise," he said. He did not elaborate.

Hedberg said Stena was still confident that the venture would be cleared before the high season. "However if there is a delay I guess we have to live with it," he added. But he noted that the deal had been announced already in October.
"We have a very high preparedness to start as soon as we get permission to start," he said.
EU sources said the Commission was concerned that a link between (P&0) and Stena line AB of Sweden may create a duopoly in cross-channel transport.
Three authorities have to sanction the proposed joint venture before it can proceed -- the European Commission, the British government, and the French government.
Stena said on Monday the French government had given its approval.
